sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: 💾 Save configuration now also saves your workspace — the things you built up by using the script rather than by opening a settings dialog. Above all your PINNED FILTER LIST, which you edit from inside the ⚙️ Settings dialog via 🔧 Edit Pinned Filter List and which therefore always looked like part of the configuration, and was not in the file. Also: which columns you have hidden on each page type (the 👁️ Visible menu's own memory, each sub-table included), your filter history, the Statistics- and Load-dialog positions and sizes, the Settings- and ChangeLog-dialog sizes, the Settings dialog's column widths and which of its sections you leave open, the 📊 dropdown's collapsed sections, and the shared library's display preferences. 📂 Load configuration restores all of it and tells you, group by group, what it restored. Moving to a second browser or a new profile no longer means re-hiding columns one page type at a time.

Column visibility now travels per sub-table as well as per page type. A page that renders several tables keeps a separate visibility state for each, and those states are found by sweeping storage rather than by guessing their names, so nothing is silently left out of the file.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: The file-format version moved from 1 to 2, and reading across the two works in both directions. A file saved by an earlier version imports exactly as before — your column visibility, pinned filters and window positions are left as they are here, rather than being cleared by a file that has no opinion about them. A file saved by a newer version imports everything this one understands and leaves the rest alone. The summary says which of the two happened, so "my window positions did not come across" is never a mystery.
The export dialog's FILE METADATA block now counts the workspace keys alongside the settings keys, so you can see before saving whether the file contains what you expect.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: A configuration file can no longer write to anything outside the settings and workspace this script owns. Every key in the file is checked against the list of things that are importable at all, and anything else is reported as skipped rather than stored — so a file that has been hand-edited, or picked up from somewhere unfamiliar, cannot reach into this installation's own bookkeeping.

The record of which one-time settings repairs this installation has already run is deliberately NOT in the file. Carrying it across would tell a browser that still needs the repair that it had already had it, and would offer to undo a repair that never ran there.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: ❓ Help's SAVE / LOAD CONFIGURATION section now lists what the file carries and what it does not, explains reading an older or newer file, and notes that saved window positions are clamped to the window they are restored into — so a file written on a large monitor cannot strand a dialog off-screen on a small one.
